newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gorbachev mourns Afghan protege Najibullah.
newsitem.headline: Gorbachev mourns Afghan protege Najibullah.

text.p: Mikhail Gorbachev on Friday condemned as a "lynching" the killing of former Afghan president Najibullah, the man installed as Afghan leader in 1987 during the Soviet occupation of the country.

The former Soviet president, ousted from the Kremlin months before his protege's reign in Kabul was cut short in 1992, told Ekho Moskvy radio that Najibullah had played a "decisive role" in negotiating the withdrawal of Moscow's forces in 1989.

Gorbachev, who now espouses free market policies, said Najibullah, a diehard communist dubbed the "Butcher of Kabul", had "understood the destructiveness for his country of the socialist path of development".
"It pains me to receive this news," Gorbachev said. "Najibullah was a serious politician and a reliable man."
"This was a lynching and some sort of savagery," he said.
The bodies of Najibullah and his brother were strung up at the gates of Kabul's presidential palace overnight after the Taleban militia took control of the city.

Najibullah, who headed the brutal KGB-style Khad secret police after the 1979 Soviet invasion, had been sheltering in a U.N. compound in Kabul since he was overthrown by Islamic Mujahideen guerrilla forces in 1992.
